result.rationale: The diff shows `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` in embed.js — a substring check of e.origin against the discourseUrl global. If the operator configures discourseUrl without a scheme (e.g. 'forum.example.com') or in a form that doesn't literally contain the origin string, all resize postMessages are silently rejected and the iframe keeps its default height. The mechanism is verifiable in the added code; severity depends on configuration, so confidence is moderate.

judged_text: The origin check `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` rejects valid messages whenever the configured discourseUrl lacks a trailing slash or uses a scheme/port variation (e.g. `https://forum.example.com` vs origin `https://forum.example.com` matches, but any path suffix or trailing-slash mismatch like `http://x/` vs origin `http://x` still passes while a discourseUrl without scheme fails all), and the resize handler does nothing when `e.data.height` is 0 or falsy. Embed sites where the configured discourseUrl string doesn't contain the exact origin substring never receive resize messages, so the iframe stays at its default height and content is clipped — the failure is silent with no console error or user-visible hint.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the origin gate is `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) return;`, which *accepts* common trailing-slash/path differences (e.g., `discourseUrl = "http://x/"` and `e.origin = "http://x"` yields index 0, so it does not reject). The finding’s main claim that missing trailing slash or path suffix causes valid messages to be rejected is not supported by the shown logic. The note about `e.data.height` being falsy (e.g., 0) preventing resize is true (`&& e.data.height`), but that’s not the stated failure mode and isn’t clearly a real defect from the diff alone.
